question: Retain or reject machinery06 attempt02 for visible connected-construction gain without receiving pose/geometry damage?
role: independent visual/evidence reviewer; root adjudicates other roles
summary: Retain a modest additive gain. Neck receiver holes become seated spindle/housing assemblies and leg centers gain cast mass around retained rods. Improvement is easiest to see in regional PBR and neck grazing clay. Matched whole-bird clay/PBR shows a small change, not a major likeness advance. Toe couplings are effectively concealed, and flank construction remains sparse against locked canon.

verified.source_resolution_note: Worker source JPG is an LFS pointer; exact hash-matching source binary inspected in architect worktree. No substitution.

three_largest_remaining_exposed_mechanis.gap: Canon has a dense, recessed but readable connected bank of actuators, brackets, collars and dark transmission bodies. Candidate still exposes a sparse wire/brace cage with isolated rings; much new flank volume is hidden in front/profile and whole views.
three_largest_remaining_exposed_mechanis.corrective_operator: A flank-specific connected transmission operator: use retained CG shield03 left/right flank barrel and piston endpoints plus CG1c hip concentric hinge centers as fixed receivers; build stepped cast housings, forked terminal yokes and two short visibly connected return paths on the camera-facing flank. Put readable major volume into the existing pocket, below the shield and behind breast; preserve body06 neck corridor and every original transform/visibility. No floating washers or extra microdetail until complete-bird profile/35-degree clay shows gain.

three_largest_remaining_exposed_mechanis.gap: Large flat rail strips and simple washer-like joint faces still dominate. Added dark cases fill centers but do not create the canon layered segmented bearing/actuator construction.
three_largest_remaining_exposed_mechanis.corrective_operator: Rework only CGM06 new leg cases/races into stepped sectional casts with forked ends, distinct concentric flanges and short side-fed collars tied to the unchanged knee/hock/ankle centers. Keep silhouette and stance fixed; evaluate at whole-bird scale before adding pins.

three_largest_remaining_exposed_mechanis.gap: Smooth instep and broad toe shells conceal the new root manifolds; the foot still reads as a simple continuous armored shoe rather than separate articulated mechanisms rooted into toes.
three_largest_remaining_exposed_mechanis.corrective_operator: Add visible compact dorsal/lateral digit-root collars and knuckle housings that bridge unchanged ankle receiver to existing proximal CGF03 toe-shell roots. Keep claw tips, toe pose and historical shells intact. Judge the same feet and whole views; concealed couplings do not count as gain.

exact_next_corrective_operator: Flank connected-transmission operator described in rank 1, after integration of body06 and metal05. Freeze completed receiving native; at most two focused attempts with same-camera whole PBR/clay and flank regional pairs. Preserve all original stance/armor/head transforms. Retain current neck and leg additions provisionally; no broad regeneration.
material_vs_geometry: Geometry gain is supported by clay and same-material before/after regional views. Green armor, bright feet, dark core response and optic state are inherited temporary bindings and are not machinery06 color decisions. Metal05 rerouting must be reviewed separately and cannot substitute for missing articulated geometry.
strongest_surviving_objection: At full-bird scale connected-construction gain remains small; new case bulk can read as another smooth strip rather than recognizable layered machinery. The front/profile clay pairs make the limited gain especially clear.
